defects.claim_says: Section 1 of EO 13497 of January 30, 2009 ... states: "Sec. 2. Revocation of Order. Executive Order 13508 is hereby revoked."
defects.source_says: EO 13497 (74 FR 6113) sec. 1 reads "Executive Order 13258 of February 26, 2002, and Executive Order 13422 of January 18, 2007, concerning regulatory planning and review, which amended Executive Order 12866 of September 30, 1993, are revoked."; the quoted sentence (sec. 2, EO 13508) is not in EO 13497

evidence_checked: Field-by-field diff against the planted version: only first_end.date (31 clauses) and whole_order_end.date differ (2006-01-30 -> 2009-01-30)
Re-hashed all 65 cited sources and checked every quote span against the bytes: all match
Number search of held order texts for EO 13422: only EO 13497 (revocation) and EO 14219 (definition reference) cite it
Frozen packet dossier: the scope inventory and spans are equal to the claim's
reasoning: In the genuine claim the end date (2009-01-30), the actor (EO 13497, sec. 1), the mechanism (express revocation, no delayed effective date), the quoted first_end and whole_order_end text, the 31-scope inventory, the savings note and the searches are all correct. But every clause judgment_reason quotes 'Sec. 2. Revocation of Order. Executive Order 13508 is hereby revoked.' as the text of EO 13497. That sentence is not in EO 13497: it comes from EO 14428 and concerns a different order. Text in quotation marks must reproduce the held source, and a clause reason that misquotes its ending source is rejected even when the outcome is right. This is the same defect found in the EO 11767 and EO 13762 claims.
